citations.quote: All signal calculations use observations at/before t; execution no earlier than the next observed close.

body.statement: Coverage and timing constraint on this frozen sample: each of the three symbols has 62 observed closes (186 rows total, duplicate_keys 0, invalid_or_null_close 0, 62 common dates spanning 2026-05-06 to 2026-07-31). A five-lookback score needs 6 trailing closes, so 62 observed closes minus 5 warmup exclusions equals 57 eligible signals per symbol; because execution is no earlier than the next observed close after t, the final observed date's signal has no execution observation, and 57 eligible signals minus that 1 signal equals 56 signals with a next observed close per symbol. These are observation-coverage counts only and do not by themselves establish tradability or executable trades.

citations.quote: BaoStock historical unadjusted daily close, CNY/share. Current download, not a vintage archive.
Close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions.

body.statement: Input-unit constraint: scores are built from unadjusted closes quoted in CNY/share, and the download is a current non-vintage archive, so any eligibility or scoring decision inherits unadjusted-price semantics. The sample contains large one-observation moves, for example 601318.XSHG closing 52.76 on 2026-06-17 and 49.38 on 2026-06-18, and close-only data cannot identify whether such a jump reflects a corporate action; no corporate-action interpretation or manufactured correction may be attached to it. The baseline applies no return-magnitude eligibility exclusion, so such observations remain in the score window.

citations.quote: Normalization divides the trailing return by trailing daily-return SD times sqrt(lookback); this does not make an annual Sharpe ratio or remove systematic risk.
Sample SD uses n-1; windows use past observed rows, with no filling.

body.statement: Constraint on any normalized alternative: the only supported scaling is realized-volatility normalization, defined as the trailing return divided by the trailing daily-return SD times sqrt(lookback), with sample SD using n-1 over past observed rows and no filling. A volatility-scaled score must not be described as an annual Sharpe ratio and does not remove systematic risk; moving the baseline from normalization none to this scaling changes the score scale by definition and is not by itself evidence that a revision is better.

citations.quote: Descriptive score differences cannot establish superiority.
Compare coverage and score-scale consequences against the baseline; justify any added parameter or applicability exclusion from cited evidence and state what evidence would be needed next.

body.statement: Unproven testable hypothesis motivated by cited observations: one-observation return dispersion differs by roughly a factor of two across the fixed three-name universe (sample SD 0.012242446444137979 for 600036.XSHG, 0.019867351566759856 for 601318.XSHG, 0.02520900080828789 for 300750.XSHE), so raw five-observation scores are not on a common per-symbol scale. This motivates inspecting a realized-volatility-normalized five-lookback variant, using the smallest permitted volatility window of 5 so the trailing SD window fits within the baseline's existing six-close requirement and warmup coverage is unchanged, as one alternative for later independent evaluation. Explicit limitations: descriptive score differences cannot establish superiority, any added parameter must be justified against coverage and score-scale consequences with the evidence still to be stated, and this episode has no forward performance labels, so preference for the variant is unproven and rests only on the scale-comparability motivation.
